android.desc:
Most finance apps hand you a budget before you've even looked around. You set limits, try to stick to them, and halfway through the month you've already blown one. Then the app reminds you about it so you feel bad.

Cashzilla doesn't do budgets. There's nothing to configure and nothing judging your spending. It just keeps an honest record of what's actually going on with your money.

See where your money went this month. See what's about to happen before it does: rent, subscriptions, or that annual renewal you always forget. And see your real net worth, which now counts what you own, not just what's in your bank account.

Add stocks, ETFs and funds, or things like a house or a car. Cashzilla keeps track of what you paid, what it's worth now, and whether you're up or down. You update prices yourself. There's no live market feed.

👀 What's inside:

- Track income and expenses
- Upcoming transactions, so "spent this month" counts the rent that's due Friday
- Investments and other assets: stocks, ETFs, funds, property, or anything else worth something
- Gains and losses measured against what you paid
- Investment accounts that show your cash and holdings together
- Net worth that includes everything you own
- Accounts for checking, savings, cash, or wherever else you keep money
- A read on how fast you're spending through the month
- Categories to show where things go, with no setup required
- CSV import and export
- Multi-currency
- Dark mode

Everything stays on your phone. You don't create an account, connect a bank, or pay a subscription. There are no servers and no cloud, so your data has nowhere to go except your device.

🙅 Skip Cashzilla if you need:

- Automatic bank syncing
- Live stock prices
- Cloud backup across devices
- Shared household accounts.

But if you've tried other finance apps and given up because they felt like a second job, this one's built for the way you actually deal with money.

Cashzilla is still growing, and we read every piece of feedback: hello@cashzilla.app

quotes.text:
There's a point in every developer's life when they build their own finance app. It's a rite of passage. Mine has arrived. I built Cashzilla for three reasons: I wanted it to be genuinely free — not free-until-the-useful-parts. It's local-only: no accounts, no server, no cloud, no bank sync. Your data lives on your device and never touches mine. That's also why it's free — there's nothing running that costs me money, so there's nothing to monetize by locking features away. If that ever changes, I'll be upfront about it. I don't want a budget. I've never stuck to one and I don't want an app that makes me feel bad about that. My vision was to build a coach: something that tells me what my money is actually doing and whether it's working for me. Opening a finance app should feel give you some pleasure; if it feels like a chore, I just won't open it.
It's early, but usable: manual entry (or CSV import), accounts, scheduled/upcoming transactions, and a set of charts. I'm dogfooding it daily and releasing features every week. Right now I'm building stock/position tracking so net worth reflects everything, not just cash.

For the React Native folks: understanding expo-router and dealing with the charts pwas disproportionately painful I burned more time than I'd like to admit bouncing between libraries before landing on a Skia setup (react-native-skia + Victory Native).

I'd love feedback. You've almost certainly tried a pile of these — I'm curious what actually made you stick with …
